extracted.intended_audience: exchange legal/compliance teams, exchange management, and SEC rule reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A regulatory rule-change filing justifying new or amended exchange fees (here, connectivity and port fees) by demonstrating compliance with the Exchange Act through competition analysis, cost analysis, and allocation methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate fee constrained by significant competitive forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The Staff Guidance: an SRO should show that a proposed fee is constrained by significant competitive forces; ‘the existence of significant competition provides a substantial basis for finding that the terms of an exchange's fee proposal are equitable, fair, reasonable, and not unreasonably or unfairly discriminatory.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If competitive forces are operative, the self-interest of exchanges will constrain unreasonable behavior. The Exchange relies on market share comparisons, accessibility alternatives, and precedent case law (e.g., NetCoalition) to demonstrate competitive constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cost-based discussion when competition not persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff Guidance: ‘even where an SRO cannot demonstrate, or does not assert, that significant competitive forces constrain the fee at issue, a cost-based discussion may be an alternative basis’ to show consistency with the Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the exchange cannot show persuasive evidence of competition constraining a fee, it should provide a cost-based justification as an alternative route to demonstrate fairness and reasonableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific quantitative information to support cost-based claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff statement: ‘If an SRO seeks to support its claims that a proposed fee is fair and reasonable because it will permit recovery of the SRO's costs, . . . specific information, including quantitative information, should be provided to support that argument.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbers: aggregate annual and monthly costs, line-item cost drivers, allocation percentages, and calculations linking costs to proposed fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees should promote parity among exchange access pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fees are reasonable because they promote parity among exchange pricing for access, which promotes competition, including in the Exchanges' ability to competitively price transaction fees, invest in infrastructure, new products and other innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare proposed fees to similar connectivity/port fees charged by other exchanges with comparable market share to show parity or relative competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standards: reasonable, equitably allocated, not unfairly discriminatory, not unduly burdensome
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b) and Section 19(b) requirements that exchange fees be reasonable and equitably allocated, not designed to permit unfair discrimination, and that they not impose a burden on competition not necessary or appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing must address these statutory criteria directly and show through analysis and data how the proposed fees meet them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and disclose impact on Equity Members, including smaller members
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully and transparently assess the impact on Equity Members—both generally and in relation to other Equity Members, i.e., to assure the fee will not create a financial burden on any participant and will not have an undue impact in particular on smaller Equity Members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analysis or data showing distributional impacts across member types and sizes; explain steps taken to mitigate adverse effects on smaller participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare proposed fees to competing exchanges' fees (comparability analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes the competing exchanges' connectivity and port fees are useful examples of alternative approaches to providing and charging for access and demonstrating how such fees are competitively set and constrained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a table of competing exchanges, connection/port types, and monthly fees; cite filings/pricing schedules of those exchanges and show similarity or reasonableness relative to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show existence of practical alternatives and elasticity of demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that market participants can choose not to connect directly (use third-party resellers/service bureaus, sponsored access, or connect only to select exchanges), evidencing elasticity of demand that constrains pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples (e.g., service bureaus reselling connectivity, members not joining all exchanges, firms accessing only one exchange) and explain how these alternatives limit an exchange's ability to raise fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document that connectivity/ports are only available to Equity Members and resale practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Connectivity and ports are only available to Equity Members or service bureaus, and only an Equity Member may utilize a port; non-Member third-parties resell the Exchange's connectivity, which can constrain direct connectivity pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reseller practices, note whether the exchange charges resellers per customer, and disclose whether the exchange receives connectivity revenue from indirect connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Analysis: identify aggregate annual and monthly costs tied to service
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange calculated aggregate annual costs for 1Gb/10Gb ULL connectivity and FIX/MEO ports (specific dollar amounts and monthly equivalents) and uses these to inform proposed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit aggregate totals, monthly breakdowns, and show how proposed fees would recover a portion or all of those costs (including any margin rationale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and disclose a clear cost allocation methodology across affiliated markets and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-step allocation: (1) determine total cost for the enterprise and allocate among exchanges using factors (server counts, hardware utilization, number of members, platform-specific factors), and (2) allocate the exchange's portion among core services (connectivity, market data, transaction execution, membership services) using consistent principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the principles, factors considered, and the rationale for differing allocations across affiliated markets; show that methodology prevents double-counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent double counting between affiliated exchanges/platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation methodology ensures that no cost would be allocated twice or double-counted between the Exchange and its affiliated markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how allocations are derived from market-specific factors and audited through Finance Team consolidation and Board/committee approvals to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide line-item cost drivers and allocation percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: List individual line-item costs considered related to offering services (Human Resources, Connectivity external fees, Internet services and external market data, Data Center, Hardware/Software maintenance, Depreciation, Allocated Shared Expenses) along with allocated annual/monthly costs and percent of all for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed schedules/tables showing amounts and percentage allocations for each cost driver for each service (e.g., 10Gb ULL, 1Gb ULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document budgeting and approval process for cost allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cost Analysis: company-wide 2023 budget review process with 'bottom up' department budgets, consolidation by Finance Team, senior management review, and Board and Finance & Audit Committee approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the procedural steps, participants (department heads, Finance Team, CFO/CEO, Board committees), and timing to show governance and oversight of cost figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate Human Resources costs by employee time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers assign percentage of time for each employee and allocate that time among exchanges and then into service buckets (e.g., network connectivity, ports). Example allocations: 58% for 10Gb ULL and 2.0% for 1Gb per relevant employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain frequency (twice a year and as needed), which departments are involved, and that employees are 100% allocated to avoid double counting; document employee-by-employee allocations for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply service-specific allocation principles (e.g., fixed costs weighted toward connectivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed costs not driven by client activity (e.g., data center costs) were allocated more heavily to physical connectivity (example: 60.0% to 10Gb ULL connectivity), with smaller allocations to FIX and MEO ports and remaining to other services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State rationale for allocating particular cost types to services based on their 'nature and closeness' to the service provided; provide percentage rules used for each cost driver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge interdependence of services and exercise reasonable judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Because transaction execution, market data, membership services, and connectivity are interdependent, the allocation of costs to each service required judgment and weighting based on reasonable estimates; there is no standardized methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the interdependencies and document the reasonableness checks and consistent application of judgment in the allocation methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context/history of prior pricing decisions for parity explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain historical pricing behavior (e.g., new exchanges offering discounted/free services at launch and legacy exchanges having set higher baseline fees prior to Revised Review Process) to justify the need for fee changes to achieve parity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use launch pricing history, membership growth rationale, and comparisons to legacy exchanges to show why fee changes are appropriate now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculate and disclose projected impact and reasons for cost variances across affiliated exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain differences in cost growth and levels among affiliated exchanges (e.g., MIAX PEARL's higher costs due to operating two markets, hardware refreshes, greater development effort), and confirm no double-counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Form 1 comparisons, explain unique drivers (number of markets, refresh projects), and show how these feed into the specific cost allocations and fee proposals.
